review.brief:
Review RM35-clock-add-bogota-time-package (tier 1 of RM35), module `clock`. Read the DIFF (main...HEAD), not the whole repo.

WHAT TO VALIDATE
1. Boundary: internal/clock imports stdlib `time` and NOTHING else, in every file including tests' non-test siblings. This is the module's defining constraint (D2) and owner decision D10 removed the one proposed exception (time/tzdata). An extra import is a blocker finding.
2. CalendarDay correctness (design D7) — the highest-risk item in the tier. It must reproduce all THREE existing truncators exactly: analytics.calendarDay (internal/analytics/consumed.go:79) and gateway.startOfDay (internal/gateway/handlers/history.go:61) when passed time.UTC, and telemetry.dateOnly (internal/telemetry/service.go:559) for any loc. Read those three and check the equivalence yourself. An off-by-one shifts day attribution across telemetry, analytics and charging once tiers 3/4/6 adopt it.
3. Zone() panics at init and does NOT fall back to UTC (owner decision D11). A silent fallback is a blocker.
4. Test QUALITY by reading (never by running): do the tests assert the expected values design.md's Test Contract authored BEFORE the implementation, or do they merely restate what the code does? The contract cases are the UTC self-truncation, the Bogota cross-day, the two America/New_York DST cases, and the LoadOrDefault table including the "" -> UTC and "Local" -> host-local gotchas.
5. Scope: this tier adopts clock NOWHERE (D4). Any edit to telemetry/analytics/app/gateway/config is out of scope and a blocker. Confirm zero adopters outside internal/clock.
6. Docs (D3): the full rule is in ai/go-conventions.md beside the units rule; CLAUDE.md holds a ONE-LINE pointer, not a restatement; root AGENTS.md has the new ai/go-conventions.md pointer; internal/clock/AGENTS.md states the stdlib-time-only rule and forbids non-time helpers; README's structure tree and architecture table include internal/clock and do not overclaim adoption. CLAUDE.md's docs-track-structural-change rule makes stale structure docs incomplete work.
7. Anti-gaming: no acceptance criterion weakened or deleted; no task marked done that is not; T1/T2 must be awaiting-user-verification, NOT done, until the owner reports the suite.
8. No database object exists in this tier — confirm none was introduced.

TEST-EXECUTION-POLICY (verbatim): Claude writes tests but never runs the suite — never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards make ui-guard / i18n-guard / money-guard. The owner runs the suite and reports results; work that is complete but unexecuted is awaiting-user-verification, never done, and a passing suite is recorded as the owner's report, never claimed by the assistant.

SIGNAL PROVENANCE — assistant-run vs owner-reported:
- ASSISTANT-RUN (leader, T8): go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l internal/clock/, make ui-guard, make i18n-guard, make money-guard, openspec validate --strict, the import-block check and the zero-adopter grep. All passed.
- OWNER-REPORTED: go test ./internal/clock/... and go test ./... — PENDING at the time this brief was written. Judge test quality by reading the test files, not by running them.

PERFORMANCE-PROFILE (verbatim): read-heavy — read performance is mandatory over write performance; writes are mostly done by pollers at midnight, so denormalizing, indexing aggressively, and precomputing for reads is acceptable — never at the cost of the modular-monolith boundaries or module data ownership. (This tier is pure in-memory functions on no hot path; note if you disagree.)
